records.summary: The records show 675 Jackson St is in the Chinatown Visitor Retail (CVR) District where a restaurant use on the first story is principally permitted per Planning Code § 811, though the pathway rules note that hours extending beyond 11 p.m. would require conditional use review. The site history shows one 1999 Planning approval confirming restaurant use as permitted. The block is exceptionally dense with food and beverage activity: 65 registered food/drink businesses within 500 ft, 34 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 ft (109 within 1,000 ft), and undue concentration flagged. The nearby base rate over the last 5 years shows 7 approvals (1 outright, 6 with conditions) against 4 withdrawals and 0 denials among 11 dated use decisions within 1,000 ft—a 63.6% approval rate—indicating that restaurant projects in this CVR and adjacent CRNC area do secure approval but often with operating conditions.

flags.flag: Zoning: Restaurant on first story principally permitted in CVR District per Planning Code § 811; standard daytime hours presumed compliant.
Hours constraint: CVR hours rule treats 6 a.m.–11 p.m. as principally permitted and 11 p.m.–2 a.m. as conditional; the pathway could not determine status because no closing time was given.
Site is in the Group Housing Special Use District and Priority Equity Geographies SUD; neither restricts restaurant use.
Extreme density: 65 food/drink businesses within 500 ft and 34 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 ft (109 within 1,000 ft); undue-concentration flag raised.

Immediately adjacent addresses (667–699 Jackson, 960 Grant) host multiple long-standing full-service restaurants with ABC Type 41 licenses, confirming this block as an established restaurant corridor.
Base rate within 1,000 ft: N=11 dated use decisions over 5 years; 7 approved (1 outright, 6 with conditions), 4 withdrawn, 0 denied; 63.6% approval rate.

One bar CUA on Wentworth Pl (21 m away) approved with 4 p.m.–2 a.m. hours and standard three-year validity/diligent-pursuit conditions; one restaurant CUA at 650 Jackson (54 m) approved with 7 a.m.–1…
Two small self-service restaurant applications (631–641 Jackson, 735 Jackson) were denied or required CUA; full-service restaurants have been approved ministerially on this block.
The 1999 site history record (MA9901227) states full-service restaurants are permitted in CVR per § 811.42; the concept's retail-to-restaurant change of use aligns with that precedent.

data_gaps: No ABC conditions text is exposed for the 38 active licenses within 500 ft, so proximity restrictions or pending protests are unknown.
The pathway says hours beyond 11 p.m. are conditional but could not classify this concept because no closing hour was stated; confirm intended hours to determine if a CUA is needed.
No hearing transcripts or vote tallies are available for the nearby CUA approvals, so the basis for conditions (e.g., hours limits) is not shown.
The Group Housing SUD and Priority Equity Geographies SUD overlay citations do not explain their rules; the records confirm they exist but not whether they affect this restaurant.

comparables.why_comparable: Conditional Use Authorization for a limited restaurant upgrading to full restaurant on the same block (650 Jackson St, 54 meters away) in the adjacent CRNC District. Same retail-to-restaurant use change pattern via CB3P streamlined process.
comparables.key_takeaway: Approved with conditions after 5 months (filed May 2019, decided Oct 2019). Hours limited to 7:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. daily. Standard eating and drinking operational conditions plus odor control and community liaison officer applied.

comparables.why_comparable: Conditional Use Authorization for retail-to-restaurant conversion in the CVR District at 838 Grant Ave (125 meters away). Same zoning district and change-of-use type, reducing retail square footage to create restaurant space.
comparables.key_takeaway: Approved with conditions after 6 months (filed Aug 2021, decided Mar 2022). Hours limited to 6:00 a.m. to midnight. Included bicycle parking requirement, plus standard noise, odor control, sidewalk maintenance, community liaison and three-year validity/diligent-pursuit conditions.

comparables.why_comparable: Conditional Use Authorization for restaurant with beer/wine service at 150 Waverly Pl (127 meters away) in CRNC District. Same CB3P streamlined review, full-service restaurant with commercial kitchen.
comparables.key_takeaway: Approved with conditions after 6 months (filed Nov 2019, decided May 2020). Hours limited to 7:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. daily. Standard eating and drinking use conditions, odor control, community liaison and three-year validity applied.

comparables.why_comparable: Conditional Use Authorization for limited restaurant to full restaurant change at 735 Jackson St (78 meters away, same block) in CRNC District. Filed in association with Type 41 ABC license application.
comparables.key_takeaway: Withdrawn after 14 months (filed Apr 2022, withdrawn Jun 2023). No conditions or reasons documented. This withdrawal on the same block signals potential issues with limited-to-full restaurant upgrades in CRNC versus CVR where the subject site sits.

comparables.why_comparable: Conditional Use Authorization for limited restaurant to full restaurant at 533 Jackson St (160 meters away) in CRNC District via CB3P process. Ground floor and basement similar to subject concept.
comparables.key_takeaway: Approved without additional operating conditions after 22 months (filed Jun 2016, decided Apr 2018). Long timeline but clean approval demonstrates that change-of-use from limited restaurant to restaurant is approvable in the corridor.

comparables.why_comparable: ABC Type 41 referral for existing restaurant at 622 Jackson St (83 meters away, same block) in CRNC District. Agency referral showing Planning approval of beer/wine licenses in the immediate vicinity.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 20 days (filed May 2023, decided May 2023). Recommendation noted continuation of existing restaurant use as conditionally permitted in CRNC per § 812 and 178. Shows streamlined ministerial pathway for ABC referrals on established restaurants.

comparables.why_comparable: ABC Type 41 referral at 960 Grant Ave (6 meters away, essentially adjacent) in CVR District. Existing restaurant (Hong Kong Clay Pot) with continuation of use under § 811 and 178.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 13 days (filed Feb 2019, decided Mar 2019). Immediate neighbor shows restaurant use is established as conditionally permitted in CVR with standard eating/drinking operating conditions per § 202.2(a).

comparables.why_comparable: Health Department restaurant referral at 801 Kearny St (114 meters away) in CCB District. Only denial in the candidate set, important to understand failure mode.
comparables.key_takeaway: Denied after 38 months (filed Jun 2016, denied Aug 2019). Agency referral for health permit; no reason documented. Extended timeline suggests unresolved building or code compliance issues rather than use-type opposition. Shows that building readiness is critical.

comparables.why_comparable: ABC Type 41 referral at 57 Columbus Ave (175 meters away) in CRNC District for restaurant operating as bona fide eating place. Shows continuation-of-use approvals for restaurants.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 4 days (filed Apr 2023, decided Apr 2023). Approved as continuation of existing legal non-conforming restaurant use permitted under § 180, demonstrating ministerial pathway for established restaurant operations.

patterns.pattern: Restaurant Conditional Use Authorizations in CVR and adjacent CRNC districts were approved with standard hours limited to 10:00 p.m. or midnight closing. Three approved CVR/CRNC restaurants imposed 7:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m. or 6:00 a.m.–midnight limits.

All restaurant CUAs imposed standard three-year validity with building permit issuance requirement and diligent pursuit conditions, plus standard eating/drinking use operational conditions: sidewalk maintenance within one-block radius, soundproofing, odor control, and hidden trash/recycling storage.
Community liaison officer appointment prior to building permit issuance was a universal condition across restaurant CUAs in CVR and CRNC districts within this corridor.

Change-of-use from limited restaurant to full restaurant or retail to restaurant required Conditional Use Authorization in CRNC and CVR (per §§ 811, 812) but followed the CB3P streamlined review pathway, with timelines of 5–6 months to decision when successful.

ABC license referrals for existing restaurants were approved ministerially within 2–3 weeks as agency referrals. Planning recommended approval as continuation of conditionally permitted use without requiring new CUA hearings.
Odor control equipment with manufacturer specifications on building permit plans was required for all full-kitchen restaurant approvals; ducting could not be applied to primary façade.

approval_signals: Retail-to-restaurant change of use on ground/first floor in CVR District aligns with principally permitted pathway under Planning Code § 811 for standard daytime hours
Immediate block (Jackson St corridor) has multiple approved full-service restaurants within 50–125 meters in both CVR and CRNC districts
CB3P streamlined review accelerated recent restaurant CUAs to 5–6 month timelines when applications were complete
No alcohol service eliminates Type 41 ABC license coordination and undue-concentration concerns despite 34 active licenses within 500 feet
Agency referrals for existing restaurants approved ministerially within 2–3 weeks shows departmental support for restaurant use on this corridor
denial_signals: One withdrawal at 735 Jackson (78 m, same block) for limited-to-full restaurant in CRNC after 14 months suggests potential complications though no reason was documented
One health referral denial at 801 Kearny after 38 months indicates building readiness (mechanical, plumbing, code compliance) can stall or kill projects even when use is permitted
Extreme density (65 food/drink businesses within 500 ft) and undue-concentration flag may prompt additional scrutiny if alcohol service is added later
Hours extending past 11:00 p.m. would trigger conditional use review even in CVR where daytime restaurant is principally permitted

risk.concept_summary: Restaurant with full commercial kitchen and tenant improvements, converting a retail space at 675 Jackson St in the Chinatown Visitor Retail (CVR) District; no alcohol service, recorded music only.

overall.next_step: Provide the three missing inputs—whether the business is formula retail, the total floor area in square feet, and the closing hour—to Planning so the zoning pathway can be determined; once those are known, file for SF business registration, then DPH health plan check and building permit application…

approvals.summary: Zoning status is insufficient information because formula retail, use size and hours were not provided; CVR § 811 permits a first-story restaurant by right under 2,500 sq ft closing by 11 p.m., but triggers conditional use if formula, ≥2,501 sq ft, or past 11 p.m.

findings.text: Restaurant use on the first story is principally permitted in the CVR Chinatown Visitor Retail District under Planning Code § 811, in force from January 14, 2024.

CVR § 811 hours rule treats 6 a.m.–11 p.m. as principally permitted and 11 p.m.–2 a.m. as conditional use; the concept gives no closing time, so the pathway could not decide whether a conditional use authorization is needed.

CVR § 811 prohibits formula retail and requires conditional use for restaurant uses of 2,501 square feet or larger; the description does not state chain affiliation or floor area, so the pathway could not decide.
The 1999 site-history agency referral (MA9901227) at this address confirmed that full-service restaurants are permitted in CVR per § 811.42, establishing continuity of restaurant use at the parcel.
Within 1,000 feet, 7 of 11 dated use decisions (N=11, last 5 years) were approved (1 outright, 6 with conditions), 4 withdrawn, 0 denied; the approval rate is 63.6%.

approvals.summary: Health permit to operate is allowed; issued after plan check and final inspection without a hearing, and the health application is referred to Planning for zoning sign-off.

findings.text: A restaurant with a full kitchen needs a health permit to operate, issued by SF Department of Public Health after plan review, equipment and finish approval, and pre-opening inspection; the permit is ministerial.
DPH health permit applications for bars and restaurants are sent to the Planning Department for zoning review under the city's interagency referral process.
Adjacent addresses at 960 Grant (6 m) and 650 Jackson (54 m) hold active health permits for full-service restaurants, confirming the use is established on this block.

approvals.summary: Building permit with change of use is further review; a retail-to-restaurant change of use per Planning Code § 102 requires a building permit, which must conform to the Planning Code before DBI will issue it, and the permit is referred to Planning for zoning sign-off.

findings.text: Retail to restaurant is a change of use under Planning Code § 102, as stated by the applicant's description of the existing space.

The proposed occupancy group is not established because the description does not state whether the space is for fewer than 50 occupants; a restaurant under 50 is Group B, 50 or more is Assembly A-2, and a change of occupancy depends on comparing the proposed group to the existing one.
Tenant improvements for a retail-to-restaurant conversion trigger a building permit routed to Planning under Planning Code § 175(a) for zoning conformity review before DBI may issue the permit.

Nearby restaurant conversions at 650 Jackson (54 m, 2019 CUA) and 838 Grant (125 m, 2021 CUA) both required Planning conditional use review for retail-to-restaurant changes in the CVR and adjacent CRNC districts.

could_not_establish.question: Whether the business is part of a chain that shares its name, look or menu with other locations (formula retail); CVR § 811 prohibits formula retail outright.
The total floor area of the restaurant space in square feet; CVR § 811 requires conditional use for restaurant uses of 2,501 sq ft or larger.
could_not_establish.ask: The applicant or the lease documents

could_not_establish.question: The closing hour each day; CVR § 811 treats 6 a.m.–11 p.m. as principally permitted and 11 p.m.–2 a.m. as conditional use.

The proposed occupant load (number of seats or persons) to determine Building Code occupancy group (Group B if under 50, Assembly A-2 if 50 or more) and whether a Fire Department place-of-assembly permit is needed.
could_not_establish.ask: The architect's occupant-load calculation on the building permit plans

could_not_establish.question: The existing occupancy group of the retail space; only the Certificate of Occupancy on file at DBI or an inspection shows it, and the change-of-occupancy answer depends on comparing existing to proposed.
could_not_establish.ask: SF Department of Building Inspection records or a site visit by a code consultant

could_not_establish.question: The construction scope and valuation for the tenant improvement work; DPH plan-check fees and building permit fees are calculated as a percentage of construction cost.
could_not_establish.ask: The general contractor's cost estimate or the architect's construction drawings

could_not_establish.question: Whether the kitchen hood and ventilation system will discharge to the roof or sidewall, and whether odor control equipment is required; DPH and the Bay Area Air Quality Management District enforce these rules.
could_not_establish.ask: The mechanical engineer's hood and exhaust design on the building permit plans

filing_playbook.action: Confirm in writing with SF Planning whether the concept as described—independent restaurant, floor area, and closing hour—requires a Conditional Use Authorization or is principally permitted in CVR.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit a written inquiry to SF Planning's information desk or pre-application meeting request stating: proposed use is a non-formula retail restaurant at 675 Jackson St (CVR District) on the first story, converting from retail, with [state square footage] and closing at [state hour]. Ask whether Planning Code § 811 permits the use as of right or requires conditional use for size, hours or formula retail, and request written confirmation before filing permits. Attach the 1999 precedent (MA9901227) showing restaurant use was permitted at this address.

filing_playbook.action: Form the legal entity (LLC or corporation) with the California Secretary of State and obtain a federal EIN from the IRS.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File Articles of Organization (LLC-1, $70) or Articles of Incorporation (ARTS-GS, $100) online at the CA Secretary of State bizfile portal. Within 90 days file the Statement of Information ($20 LLC, $25 corporation). Once the entity is registered, apply for an Employer Identification Number (EIN) online at IRS.gov (free, issued same day Mon–Fri). The EIN and entity name are required for the business registration, bank account, seller's permit, and all city permits.

filing_playbook.action: Register the business with SF Treasurer & Tax Collector to obtain a Business Account Number (BAN) and register for the California seller's permit with CDTFA.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File online at sftreasurer.org for the SF Business Registration Certificate ($55–$700 tiered by gross receipts, plus $4 state fee). The BAN is required by every other city department. In parallel, register online at the CA Department of Tax and Fee Administration for the seller's permit (free; required to sell food and drink). Both take 1–5 days. If the public-facing restaurant name differs from the legal entity name, file a Fictitious Business Name statement with the SF County Clerk and publish it in a court-approved newspaper within 45 days.

filing_playbook.action: Submit DPH health plan check application and building permit application with change-of-use routing to Planning in parallel.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: For DPH: apply online at sfdph.org/ehsportal with your BAN, Location ID (LIN) and EIN. Submit two sets of scaled floor plans, equipment layout, menu, finishes schedule, and hood/ventilation drawings. State that the project is a retail-to-restaurant change of use with full commercial cooking. DPH will route the application internally and assign a plan reviewer; fee is $828–$2,207 depending on scope (paid at application). For DBI: file a building permit application with tenant-improvement plans stamped by a licensed architect, showing the change of use from retail to restaurant. DBI will route the application to Planning under Planning Code § 175(a) for zoning conformity review and to DPH for concurrent review. State on the permit that the existing use is retail and the proposed use is restaurant, and that the project is subject to the health plan check already filed. Include mechanical,…

filing_playbook.action: Obtain a Certified Food Protection Manager certificate (one manager) and enroll all employees in California Food Handler Card training.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: At least one owner or manager must pass an ANSI-accredited food safety exam (ServSafe, Prometric, NRFSP, 360training) within 60 days of opening; the certificate is valid 5 years and DPH asks for it at the pre-opening inspection ($100–$250, 1–14 days). Every employee who handles food must obtain a California Food Handler Card within 30 days of hire (online course, $7–$15, valid 3 years). Keep certificates on site for health inspections.

filing_playbook.action: Respond to DPH and DBI plan-check corrections and coordinate Fire Department hood and ventilation sign-off; schedule pre-final and final inspections at ~80% and 100% construction complete.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Work with your architect and mechanical engineer to address DPH and DBI comments on finishes, equipment, plumbing fixture counts, hood suppression system, grease interceptor, and ADA compliance. The Fire Department reviews the hood suppression system as part of the building permit; if the occupant load is 50 or more, a Place of Assembly permit is required from SFFD ($446). Schedule a DPH pre-final inspection at ~80% complete and a final pre-opening inspection when all equipment is installed, surfaces sealed, hand sinks operational, and hot water available; the health permit is issued after the final inspection passes. Schedule DBI final inspection to obtain the Certificate of Final Completion; Planning's zoning sign-off must be complete before DBI will finalize.

filing_playbook.action: Register with CA EDD for payroll taxes, obtain workers' compensation insurance, and subscribe to organics recycling service (SB 1383) before the first employee is hired or food waste is generated.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register as an employer at EDD's e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying more than $100 in wages (free, online, 1–7 days). Obtain workers' compensation insurance from a licensed carrier or State Fund before hiring the first employee (mandatory from day one; quote through a broker). Contact your waste hauler (Recology in SF) to add organics (green bin) collection for commercial food generators per SB 1383; no permit required but the service must be in place before the health inspection.

filing_playbook.action: File for exterior sign permit with Planning and DBI, and obtain ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses for recorded music.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: For signage: submit sign drawings to Planning for design review (size, illumination, historic-district compliance) and to DBI for permit issuance; fee is $300–$1,500, 7–45 days. For music: register online at ASCAP.com and BMI.com for blanket public performance licenses (formula-based fee, ~$300–$2,500/year each, effective immediately). Federal copyright law requires both licenses to play recorded music in a commercial space; the two catalogs do not overlap. Alternatively subscribe to a licensed commercial music service (e.g., Soundtrack Your Brand) that includes performance rights.

timeline_cost.notes: The timeline and cost cover the two approvals in the entitlement path (health permit to operate and building permit with change of use) plus their prerequisites, from entity formation through final inspection. The day range is the time to obtain those approvals when they are granted: health permit 14–45 days after plan check (21–60 days), building permit 14–120 days including Planning's zoning referral (14–90 days). If the zoning review determines that a Conditional Use Authorization is required (because the concept is formula retail, ≥2,501 sq ft, or closes after 11 p.m.), add 120–300 days and $3,100–$15,000 for the CUA hearing, which is not included here because the pathway status is insufficient information. The cost range includes: CA SOS LLC/corp ($70–$150), SF business registration ($55–$700), DPH health plan check ($828–$2,500), health permit application ($470–$1,000), building permit ($800–$15,000), Fire place-of-assembly permit if occupant load ≥50 ($446–$1,500), and sign permit ($300–$1,500). Not included: construction costs, architect and engineer fees, workers' comp insurance premiums (percentage of payroll), music licenses (~$600–$5,000/year), or a CUA filing fee. The timeline assumes plans are complete and responsive to plan-check corrections; incomplete submittals or failed inspections extend the schedule by weeks to months. The one health-referral denial in the candidate set (801 Kearny, 38 months to denial) shows that building readiness is the critical path risk.
